questions.q: Did you get pocket money when you were a child?
questions.answer: Yes, a small amount each week from my father. I usually spent it on snacks or comics, but occasionally I'd save up for a new cricket bat. That was probably my first lesson in [[delayed gratification]].

questions.q: Are you good at saving money?
questions.answer: I'm getting better at it. I used to spend fairly carelessly, but now I set aside a fixed amount each month before anything else. Being [[frugal]] in small ways gives me real peace of mind.

questions.q: What do you spend most of your money on?
questions.answer: Apart from contributing to household expenses, mostly books, transport and the occasional meal out with friends. I'm also putting money aside for studying abroad, so I try not to [[splash out]] on anything unnecessary.

questions.q: Do you prefer paying in cash or by mobile?
questions.answer: Mostly by mobile these days. Mobile banking apps are hugely popular in Bangladesh, and they've [[revolutionised]] everyday payments here. Rickshaw fares and small market purchases are still usually paid in cash, though.

questions.q: Do you think schools should teach children about money?
questions.answer: Absolutely. Many young people finish school without knowing how to budget or save properly. Basic financial lessons would help them avoid debt and make [[informed decisions]] once they start earning.
